quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle completely:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more attention than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, you should pick:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on things. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
Can cause you to move into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to move into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you can't hold the turn, you may slide into another lane or off the road. Be careful when turning.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: To lower the risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of the lane where others can't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than a small problem on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to help you grip the handlebars better.
Not be worn because they make it harder to control the motorcycle.
Be worn only on cold days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to help you grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: A pre-ride check usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only needed if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It should only take a few minutes.

questions.question: Penalties for riding while impaired can include:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If convicted of impaired riding, you may face fines, license suspension, jail time, court costs, legal fees, higher insurance rates, and community service. Don't ride if you have been drinking.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose clothing made from durable materials.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem when the road is wet.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in a spot the driver cannot see. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape path.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean the same way the operator leans.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit right behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that tell drivers about road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They have white backgrounds with black letters or symbols. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many crashes happen there between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: When it is clear that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal if you are at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think your plan is obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip for motorcycle tires. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates are more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: An easy way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag on its frame.
Ride on the shoulder when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing to be more visible. Ride with your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: A motorcycle headlight:

options.text: Must be used at all times.
Must be used only between sunset and sunrise.
Does not need to be white.
Must be used only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be used at all times.
questions.explanation: Minnesota law requires you to turn on your motorcycle headlight whenever you ride.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of crashing, you should:

options.text: Keep your plans secret from other drivers.
Always ride within one foot of another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, other drivers must see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The body gets rid of almost ______ per hour.
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: Your body can remove the alcohol from about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Before every ride, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check both brake levers before every ride. Each one should feel firm and hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need regular checks?
questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous while riding.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of crashing, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about your riding if you feel okay.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can hurt your riding ability.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before your first ride. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers see you easily.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: For your safety, know what is behind you. Check your mirrors frequently as part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead when stopping takes longer. This extra distance gives you more time to react.

questions.question: What is an important benefit of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is too warm to wear in hot weather.
It protects your skin in a crash.
It should not be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your skin in a crash.
questions.explanation: A leather jacket protects your skin during a crash. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Expect it to handle exactly like your own bike.
Assume the owner checked the brakes for you.
Give yourself extra space to stop and react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself extra space to stop and react.
questions.explanation: Check a borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own bike. Ride carefully and allow yourself extra stopping distance on an unfamiliar motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand.
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You can ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Complete all passes within posted speed limits and only in legal passing zones. Only pass where it is safe and allowed.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors. This increases the chance they will see you.

questions.question: When does alcohol begin to impair your riding ability?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. Never drink before riding.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not work as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should motorcycle riders watch out for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a place to park.
Cars pulling away from the curb or parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling away from the curb or parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be cautious when passing parked cars. Vehicles may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important way to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.
